item.title: Interactive Quiz Builder for Classroom Use
item.description:
Overview

This project grew out of a simple frustration: creating engaging quizzes for students was taking far too long with existing tools. I designed and prototyped an interactive quiz builder that lets educators drag question types onto a canvas, customise feedback messages, and export a shareable link in under five minutes.

What It Does

  • Supports multiple question formats: multiple choice, true/false, short answer, and image-based prompts
  • Provides instant feedback to students with customisable explanations for each answer
  • Tracks basic completion data so teachers can identify where students are struggling

What I Learned

Building this taught me as much about instructional design as it did about interface design. Every decision — where to place a button, what language to use in error messages — had a direct impact on whether a teacher would actually use it in their classroom.

item.title: Collaborative Learning Activity Pack — Group Thinking Toolkit
item.description:
Overview

Designed for secondary school classrooms, this activity pack gives teachers a ready-to-run toolkit for structured collaborative learning. It includes facilitated discussion cards, role-assignment frameworks, and reflection prompts that guide students through group tasks without the usual chaos.

What’s Included

  • 12 discussion card sets covering STEM, humanities, and creative subjects
  • A facilitator guide with timing suggestions and differentiation tips
  • Digital versions compatible with Google Slides and Microsoft PowerPoint
  • A student self-assessment rubric aligned to collaborative skills frameworks

The Thinking Behind It

Most group work fails not because students can’t collaborate, but because the structure isn’t there to support it. This pack removes the ambiguity — every student knows their role, every group knows the goal, and the teacher has room to observe rather than manage.

item.title: Adaptive Digital Flashcard System
item.description:
Overview

This project applied the science of spaced repetition to a simple, distraction-free flashcard interface. Rather than showing cards randomly, the system schedules reviews based on how confidently a student rated their last attempt — surfacing difficult cards more often and familiar ones less frequently.

Key Features

  • Confidence-based scheduling using a simplified SM-2 spaced repetition algorithm
  • Support for text, image, and audio card types
  • Progress dashboard showing retention rates by topic
  • Offline-first design so students can study without a reliable internet connection

Why It Matters

Rote memorisation has a reputation problem — and rightfully so when done poorly. This tool aims to rehabilitate flashcard learning by making it smarter, not harder. Students who used it in a six-week pilot reported feeling more confident going into assessments.

item.title: Lesson Plan Template Library — Editable Frameworks for Educators
item.description:
Overview

Good lesson planning is invisible to students and invaluable to teachers. This library gives educators a head start with twenty professionally designed templates, each built around a specific pedagogical model and ready to adapt for any subject or year group.

Templates Included

  • Direct instruction and modelled learning
  • Inquiry-based and discovery learning
  • Flipped classroom structures
  • Project-based learning (PBL) multi-week arcs
  • Socratic seminar and discussion-based formats
  • Differentiated instruction frameworks for mixed-ability groups

Design Principles

Each template was designed with three priorities: clarity for the teacher planning the lesson, flexibility for different subjects and year levels, and usefulness as a reflection document after the lesson is taught.
